'''Knoebels Amusement Resort''' ({{IPAc-en|k|ə|ˈ|n|oʊ|b|əl|z}}) (oftened shortened to just '''Knoebels''') is a family-owned and operated [[amusement park]], [[picnic]] grove, and [[campground]] in [[Elysburg, Pennsylvania]]. Opened in 1926, it is the United States' largest free-admission park. Visitors are able to ride the park's attractions by purchasing unlimited-access wristbands, limited-access hand stamps, or books of tickets.<ref>[http://knoebels.com/index.php/rates Knoebels price page, then open "Pay One Price" tab] Retrieved 2012-02-15</ref>

The amusement park is owned and operated by the Knoebel family. The park's name has traditionally been spelled "Knoebels" without an apostrophe, and appears that way on all official park advertising and correspondence.

The park has 58 rides, including three [[wooden roller coaster]]s, three [[steel roller coaster]]s, a 1913 [[carousel]], and two [[dark ride]]s. The park and its rides have won awards from organizations such as ''[[Amusement Today]]'', [[American Coaster Enthusiasts]] (ACE), and the [[International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions]] (IAAPA).<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2014-01-08 |title=All-time Winners By Category |url=http://goldenticketawards.com/all-time-winners-by-category/#9 |access-date=2018-09-14 |work=The Golden Ticket Awards {{!}} Presented by Amusement Today |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2014, [[Travel Channel]] rated Knoebels one of their Top 10 Family Friendly Amusement Parks in the United States<ref>{{cite web |title=Top 10 Amusement Parks |url=http://www.travelchannel.com/interests/family/articles/top-10-amusement-parks |access-date=2014-07-18}}</ref>, and in 2026, [[Tripadvisor|TripAdvisor]] ranked it as the number one amusement park in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=Amusement & Water Parks - United States |url=https://www.tripadvisor.com/TravelersChoice-ThingsToDo-cAmusementWaterParks-g191 |website=www.tripadvisor.com}}</ref> 

== History ==
Knoebels is located in a small wooded valley in central Pennsylvania. In 1828, a local man by the name of Henry Knoebel purchased the land for $931 (equivalent to $32,360 in 2026). The valley, originally known as Peggy's Farm, was used as farming land until the early 1900s, when a creek-fed [[swimming hole]] was introduced. Knoebel turned the property into a popular picnic destination, attracting Sunday travelers and horse-drawn [[hayride]] wagons. Soft drinks, ice cream, and snacks were sold to visitors. As the popularity of the area (which was known as Knoebels Grove by this point) grew, the owners leased plots of land along the creeks for use as summer cottage sites. Some of these privately owned cottages still exist on the property today.

=== Development of select park features ===

In 1926, Knoebels added a restaurant, a steam-powered [[Philadelphia Toboggan Coasters]] (PTC) carousel, and a few simple games to the grove, marking the beginning of Knoebels Amusement Park. On July 4, 1926, a large concrete [[swimming pool]] was opened on the site of the original swimming hole. Featuring a filtration system that provided clean water instead of muddy creek water, the pool was named Crystal Pool. Since then, the park has developed around the pool, adding rides, games, concession stands, and other attractions.

In 1962, a campground with six sites opened behind the amusement park. As of 2004, the campground spanned {{convert|160|acre}} with 500 campsites.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knoebels Amusement Resort History |url=http://www.knoebels.com/knoebels-history.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101213175823/http://knoebels.com/knoebels-history.asp |archive-date=2010-12-13 |access-date=2011-01-25 |publisher=Knoebels.com}}</ref>

After the 1972 flood, the roller rink building was re-floored and used as a skating rink until the mid-1980s, when it was converted into the Roaring Creek Saloon. The building now contains a concession stand, an arcade, the XD Theater, and a place for live performances. 

In 1973, the Haunted Mansion dark ride opened. The ride has been recognized as one of America's best dark rides by organizations such as Dark Ride and Funhouse Enthusiasts (DAFE) and the [[National Amusement Park Historical Association]] (NAPHA).<ref>{{cite web |title=Darkride and Funhouse Enthusiasts |url=http://www.dafe.org/rides/HauntedMansionKnoebels.html |access-date=2011-03-12 |publisher=dafe.org}}</ref> In 2008, it was the subject of a one-hour documentary, "Laff In The Dark's Behind The Scenes At Knoebel's Haunted House".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dark Ride DVD Knoebels Haunted House |url=https://laffinthedark.com/mysticraft/Knoebels/khd.html |access-date=2024-06-17 |website=laffinthedark.com}}</ref>

From 2007 to 2019, the park's Grand Carousel was consistently voted the best carousel in the [[Golden Ticket Awards]]. The carousel competition was retired in 2019 because the Grand Carousel was undefeated.<ref name=":0" />

For the 2013 season, Knoebels added StratosFear, the park's tallest ride at {{convert|148|ft}}. In October of that season, Flying Turns, a wooden bobsled coaster inspired by similar early 20th century rides, opened after seven years of delays. 

In 2015, a new roller coaster named Impulse opened, replacing two former rides: Bumper Boats and Boat Tag.

In 2023, the [[Pennsylvania Trolley Museum]] acquired a trolley that had been converted into a cottage at Knoebels.<ref>{{cite web |title=Museum acquires 'rare' trolley from Knoebels Amusement Resort |url=https://www.newsitem.com/news/local/museum-acquires-rare-trolley-from-knoebels-amusement-resort/article_9385d509-aa40-5bdc-a8e7-cc404c5576cd.html |access-date=2 April 2024 |website=NewsItem|date=21 August 2023 }}</ref>

Richard “Dick” Knoebel, who was the long-standing president of the park and led many significant projects, died at the age of 87 in July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whittaker |first=Adam |date=2026-07-16 |title=Former Knoebels president Richard "Dick" Knoebel dies aged 87 |url=https://attractionsdaily.com/2026/07/dick-knoebel-2026/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Attractions Daily |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Floods ===

Because the park sits at the confluence of the [[South Branch Roaring Creek]] and [[Mugser Run]] creeks, it has suffered several major floods and a marker at the park shows the flood levels for them.

* June 1972: Resulting from [[Hurricane Agnes]],<ref name="Zyla">{{cite news |last1=Zyla |first1=Tim |title=Fifty years later: Knoebels owners reflect on experiences from Agnes |url=https://www.newsitem.com/news/local/fifty-years-later-knoebels-owners-reflect-on-experiences-from-agnes/article_b2941894-905b-5f0f-b6a6-9d16598dd879.html |work=[[The News-Item]] |date=June 23, 2022}}</ref> this was the park's worst flood. The creeks rose {{convert|6|ft}} over their banks. The flood destroyed six cottages and damaged many other buildings, including 24 of the park's then-25 rides, as well as the [[roller rink]].

* September 1975: Resulting from [[Hurricane Eloise]]<ref name="Republican Herald 2011">{{cite news |title=Damage at Knoebels close to ’72 flood mark |url=https://www.republicanherald.com/2011/09/30/damage-at-knoebels-close-to-72-flood-mark/ |work=[[Republican Herald]] |date=September 30, 2011}}</ref>

* January 1996: Resulting from a blizzard that was followed by a quick thaw<ref name="Republican Herald 2011" />

* September 2004: Resulting from [[Hurricane Ivan]]<ref name="Republican Herald 2011" />

* June 2006: Resulting from heavy rains<ref name="Republican Herald 2011" />

* September 2011: Resulting from [[Tropical Storm Lee (2011)|Tropical Storm Lee]],<ref name="Republican Herald 2011" /> this was the park's second-worst flood with waters reaching nearly as high as the 1972 flood.

* July 2018: Resulting from heavy rains and flash flooding<ref name="Tanenbaum">{{cite news |last1=Tanenbaum |first1=Michael |title=Severe flooding closes Knoebels, Hershey Park as more rain looms |url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/knoebels-hershey-park-flooding-closed-rain-pennsylvania-severe-weather/ |work=PhillyVoice |date=July 23, 2018}}</ref>

== Rides and attractions ==
=== Roller coasters ===
Knoebels has six operating roller coasters. Knoebels' two main wooden roller coasters are well-known, with Phoenix consistently rated in top ten lists and Twister ranking high as well.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wood Roller Coaster Poll 12 Year Results Table (1994–2005) |url=http://www.ushsho.com/woodpoll12yeartable2005.htm |access-date=2011-01-25 |publisher=Ushsho.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 28, 2008 |title=Golden Ticket |url=http://www.amusementtoday.com/GoldenTicket/g_ticket_wooden.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080528171109/http://www.amusementtoday.com/GoldenTicket/g_ticket_wooden.html |archive-date=2008-05-28 |access-date=2011-01-25 |publisher=Amusement Today}}</ref>

* Over the Top - [[SBF Visa Group]] - Operated for only a few weeks in 2018 before being removed due to complications
* Wipeout - Removed following the 2020 season
* The Whip - Earlier 8-car model replaced by the 12-car Whipper
* [[Bocaraca|Whirlwind]] - [[Vekoma]] - A [[Steel roller coaster|steel]] [[roller coaster]] that operated on the site of the former Jet Star coaster from 1993 to 2004. This ride was purchased from [[Playland (New York)|Playland]] in New York, where it operated from 1984 to 1992 under the same name before being moved to Knoebels. After the 2004 operating season, the ride was moved to [[Parque Diversiones]] in [[San José, Costa Rica]], where it now operates under the name Bocaraca.

=== Restaurants and food ===
Knoebels has several restaurants throughout the park. These eateries have contributed to the park winning awards from organizations which judge amusement park food, including ''Amusement Today''<nowiki/>'s Golden Ticket Award for Best Food every year from 2000 to 2012. The park tied with [[Dollywood]] in 2013, but Knoebels reclaimed the title in 2015, 2016, and 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-01-08 |title=All-time Winners By Category |url=http://goldenticketawards.com/all-time-winners-by-category/#6 |access-date=2018-09-14 |work=The Golden Ticket Awards {{!}} Presented by Amusement Today |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.knoebels.com/blog/knoebels-cesaris-pizza-reflect-on-partnership | title=Knoebels-Cesari's Pizza Reflect on Partnership | Knoebels Amusement Resort }}</ref> In 2025, ''Amusement Today'' magazine retired the Best Food contest and awarded Knoebels their "Legend" Golden Ticket Award for the category.<ref> {{Cite web |title=The Golden Ticket Awards {{!}} Presented by Amusement Today |url=https://goldenticketawards.com/ |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=The Golden Ticket Awards {{!}} Presented by Amusement Today |language=en-US}} </ref>

The park's Cesari's Pizza (now simply named Pizza)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dine |url=https://knoebels.com/dine/ |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=Knoebels Amusement Resort |language=en-US}}</ref> and the International Food Court were featured on a [[Food Network]] special. The alligator bites served at the International Food Court were selected by [[Delish.com]] as one of the top seven most daring amusement park foods.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 August 2011 |title=Amazing Amusement Park Food |url=http://www.delish.com/food-fun/amusement-park-food#fbIndex1 |work=delish.com}}</ref>

=== Three Ponds Golf Course ===
Knoebels' Three Ponds Golf Course is located roughly a quarter mile from the park and campground. It is a par 71 eighteen-hole [[golf course]] which provides two nine-hole layouts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Daily Rates & Specials – Knoebels – Free-Admission Amusement Park in Central PA with Rollercoasters, Campgrounds, Pools, Golf Courses & More! |url=http://www.knoebels.com/golf/rates-membership |work=knoebels.com |access-date=2015-04-18 |archive-date=2015-04-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150420060617/http://www.knoebels.com/golf/rates-membership |url-status=dead }}</ref> There is also a restaurant on the golf course grounds.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Nickle Plate Bar & Grill |url=http://www.knoebels.com/nickle-plate/the-nickle-plate-bar-grill |access-date=October 11, 2017 |work=knoebels.com}}</ref>

== Incidents ==

* On June 13, 2003, a man was seriously injured in a {{convert|30|ft|m|adj=on}} fall from the Scenic Skyway chairlift ride. The man was a member of a [[group home]] for [[Developmental disability|mentally disabled]] people and was riding alone. He was airlifted to a local hospital and recovered. The ride had opened to the public only two weeks before the accident. Inspectors found no problems with the ride.<ref>{{cite news |date=2003-06-13 |title=Man falls from Scenic Skyway at Knoebels |url=http://www.rideaccidents.com/2003.html#jun13 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061206085353/http://www.rideaccidents.com/2003.html#jun13 |archive-date=2006-12-06 |access-date=2007-01-04 |publisher=Ride Accidents}}</ref>
* On July 6, 2011, a young boy was found face down in the Crystal Pool. Lifeguard performed CPR on the boy, and by the time the ambulance arrived, he had obtained a heartbeat and was breathing on his own. However, he later died at [[Geisinger Medical Center]] from breathing complications. It was later determined that the child suffered from a pre-existing heart condition that is associated with [[Noonan syndrome]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Beauge |first=John |date=March 24, 2012 |title=Boy who died at Knoebels Amusement Park had undiagnosed heart problem, coroner says |url=http://www.pennlive.com/midstate/index.ssf/2012/03/boy_who_died_at_knoebels_amuse.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328041110/http://www.pennlive.com/midstate/index.ssf/2012/03/boy_who_died_at_knoebels_amuse.html |archive-date=2012-03-28 |access-date=2012-03-24 |work=Patriot News}}</ref>
* On March 26, 2015, a worker suffered cuts to the back of his head and hand after being hit by one of the Impulse coaster's trains. The ride was being tested before its public debut a month later. He was taken to a nearby hospital and recovered.<ref>{{cite news |author=Nikki Krize |date=2015-03-26 |title=Worker Hurt During Roller Coaster Testing |url=https://wnep.com/2015/03/26/worker-hurt-during-roller-coaster-testing/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190120093808/https://wnep.com/2015/03/26/worker-hurt-during-roller-coaster-testing/ |archive-date=2019-01-20 |access-date=2019-01-20 |publisher=WNEP-TV}}</ref>
* On July 16, 2016, a young boy died after he was found unresponsive in the Crystal Pool. He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was pronounced dead.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=Melissa Chan |date=12 August 2016 |title=8-Year-Old Boy Drowns in Pool at Knoebels Amusement Resort |url=https://time.com/4409627/knoebels-amusement-resort-drowning-boy/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812074134/http://time.com/4409627/knoebels-amusement-resort-drowning-boy/ |archive-date=12 August 2016 |access-date=August 12, 2016 |magazine=[[TIME]]}}</ref>
* On August 15, 2016, at around 4:30 p.m., an 11-year-old girl from [[Hellertown, Pennsylvania]] was injured when a 40-foot tree fell onto her family's campsite in a strong gust of wind. The girl, her father, and her two siblings were all taken to a nearby hospital for treatment, where she remained in critical condition.<ref>{{cite news |author=Emma Ginader |date=2016-08-18 |title=Young girl remains in critical condition after accident at Knoebels |url=https://www.dailyitem.com/news/young-girl-remains-in-critical-condition-after-accident-at-knoebels/article_65f3d708-6547-11e6-a7bf-47d0f192e25b.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711011515/https://www.dailyitem.com/news/young-girl-remains-in-critical-condition-after-accident-at-knoebels/article_65f3d708-6547-11e6-a7bf-47d0f192e25b.html |archive-date=2021-07-11 |access-date=2019-01-02 |newspaper=The Daily Item}}</ref>

* On July 15, 2023, a woman was stabbed at the campground during an altercation with another guest. After a cooler of ice water was dumped on her daughter's head, 32-year-old Jessica Bertholf grabbed a knife and tried to slash the truck tires of the person who dumped the water. The victim tried to defend herself against Bertholf, who slashed the victim across the neck with the knife. The victim survived her injuries and Bertholf was taken to jail facing charges of aggravated assault.<ref>{{cite web |date=15 July 2023 |title=One person injured, one in custody after fight at Knoebels Campground |url=https://www.wnep.com/article/news/local/columbia-county/one-person-stabbed-at-knoebels-campground-columbia-county-northumberland-county-elysburg/523-21ffce5a-e6e1-4f92-9fdc-fb450ad42a14}}</ref>

* On March 2, 1999, an attorney representing two girls who sustained injuries while riding the park's Speed Slide discovered a history of 15 complaints of injuries on the same ride. The [[tort]] lawsuit filed sought $9,200 in medical costs and at least $50,000 in [[damages]] on behalf of one girl, age 11. The suit also sought $5,300 in medical costs and at least $100,000 in damages on behalf of the other girl, age 12. Both girls had undergone emergency surgery as a result of their injuries. The park was charged with [[negligence]], failure to monitor the force of the water and its effect on riders, failure to fix defects, and failure to provide adequate warnings to riders.<ref>{{cite news |date=1999-03-02 |title=Knoebels water slide brings injuries, lawsuits |url=http://www.rideaccidents.com/1999.html#mar2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120101134450/http://www.rideaccidents.com/1999.html#mar2 |archive-date=2012-01-01 |access-date=2007-01-04 |publisher=Ride Accidents}}</ref> Both girls fully recovered.<ref>{{cite web |title=1999 Accident Reports and News |url=http://www.rideaccidents.com/1999.html#mar2 |access-date=2011-01-25 |publisher=RideAccidents.com}}</ref>

extract:
Knoebels Amusement Resort () (oftened shortened to just Knoebels) is a family-owned and operated amusement park, picnic grove, and campground in Elysburg, Pennsylvania. Opened in 1926, it is the United States' largest free-admission park. Visitors are able to ride the park's attractions by purchasing unlimited-access wristbands, limited-access hand stamps, or books of tickets.
The amusement park is owned and operated by the Knoebel family. The park's name has traditionally been spelled "Knoebels" without an apostrophe, and appears that way on all official park advertising and correspondence.
The park has 58 rides, including three wooden roller coasters, three steel roller coasters, a 1913 carousel, and two dark rides. The park and its rides have won awards from organizations such as Amusement Today, American Coaster Enthusiasts (ACE), and the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAAPA). In 2014, Travel Channel rated Knoebels one of their Top 10 Family Friendly Amusement Parks in the United States, and in 2026, TripAdvisor ranked it as the number one amusement park in the United States.
